In detail

Press coverage from 2022-2026 shows this LEA has a well-documented, repeated pattern of serious gun and gang crime concentrated in Drimnagh and the Cherry Orchard part of Ballyfermot, alongside lower-level anti-social behaviour elsewhere. The most significant recent event was the fatal shooting of 20-year-old Josh Itseli in Drimnagh on 6 May 2024, in which gunmen in a passing car opened fire before crashing; the Irish Times described 'gunfire, crashed cars, a pipe bomb and a killing' during the chaotic aftermath, with Gardai voicing concern over a 'minor gang's' access to high-powered weapons. Arrests followed in 2025 but suspects were released without charge (RTE, TheJournal.ie, May 2025). Drimnagh and neighbouring Crumlin are also historically associated with the long-running Crumlin-Drimnagh drug feud, which produced numerous gangland killings in the 2000s and is still referenced in ongoing crime reporting. Cherry Orchard, within Ballyfermot, saw well-documented multi-night disorder in early 2022, with the Irish Examiner describing 'scenes of mayhem' over 'five nights of disturbances' and residents demanding more Garda resources; two men were separately charged after an assault on Gardai in Ballyfermot in November 2022. An Irish Times feature from November 2022 quoted residents saying 'nobody wants to live here' due to persistent car theft. Bluebell has had isolated serious incidents, including a teenager left in serious condition after an assault (Irish Times, May 2023) and an earlier shooting/attempted murder at a flat complex. Organised crime remains active locally, illustrated by a €2m cannabis seizure at a Ballyfermot business in June 2025. A tragic father-and-son murder-suicide spanning Ballyfermot and Clondalkin was reported in January 2026, though this stemmed from a domestic custody dispute rather than street crime. No comparable pattern of daytime street violence was found, but the frequency and severity of gun crime and gang activity, particularly after dark, support a cautious rating. Sources checked: The Irish Times (irishtimes.com); RTE (rte.ie); TheJournal.ie (thejournal.ie); Irish Examiner (irishexaminer.com); Dublin Gazette (dublingazette.com); Dublin People (dublinpeople.com).
